lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Guided practice A: two-variable relationships and their graphs

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Use this example as the model for the guided set below.

items.prompt: A model needs 3.2 vans. How many are required?

steps: Three vans leave some load uncarried, so four are needed.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A repair service charges a $150 call-out fee plus $2 per hour. A job cost $162 in total. Which equation determines the number of hours h?
The formula A = -4bh − 5 models a design constraint, where A, b, and h are positive. Solve it for h.
Item A costs $13 each and item B costs $11 each. You may spend at most $230 in total. Which inequality expresses this constraint on the counts a and b?
A tank holds 255 litres and is filling at 5 litres per minute. After how many minutes does it hold 365 litres?
A model gives a required side length of −6 metres. How should this solution be interpreted?
choices: Reject the solution; a length cannot be negative, so it lies outside the model’s domain.
Use 6 metres, taking the absolute value.
Report −6 metres, because the algebra is correct.
Add 6 to every measurement to correct the model.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A repair service charges a $120 call-out fee plus $11 per hour. A job cost $296 in total. Which equation determines the number of hours h?
The formula A = -5bh + 1 models a design constraint, where A, b, and h are positive. Solve it for h.
Item A costs $27 each and item B costs $17 each. You may spend at most $260 in total. Which inequality expresses this constraint on the counts a and b?

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A tank holds 240 litres and is filling at 2 litres per minute. After how many minutes does it hold 266 litres?
A budget model allows 12.7 units of a product sold individually. How should this solution be interpreted?
choices: Report 12.7, because the constraint is satisfied.
Round up to 13, because 12.7 is closer to 13.
Split the order so the fractional unit is shared.
Round down to 12; buying a partial unit is not possible and 13 would exceed the budget.
